text: Every single dynamic value in Data Factory — a parameter reference, a variable, an activity output — is written in one expression language, evaluated at runtime. Start an expression with the at symbol. A literal string with no at symbol is returned exactly as written. And escape a literal at symbol itself with two of them in a row.

A bare expression keeps its original type — a number stays a number. Wrap that same expression in curly braces after the at symbol instead, and it forces the result into a string — string interpolation, genuinely useful the moment you're building a dynamic file name or a message rather than passing a value straight through untouched.

Six real categories of built-in functions worth knowing exist. Date and time for timestamp manipulation. String for text operations. Collection for arrays and objects. Logical for boolean operations. Conversion for changing types. And math for numeric work. You don't need to memorize every function — just know these six categories exist, so you know where to look.

System variables need no setup at all. Pipeline dot Pipeline returns its name. RunId identifies this specific run. TriggerTime tells you exactly when it fired. And for a schedule trigger specifically, scheduledTime and startTime can genuinely differ slightly — worth knowing before you assume they're identical.

Every activity across this entire chapter — If Condition's boolean, Switch's string, ForEach's array, Until's loop condition — is powered by this exact same expression language underneath. Chapter 4 complete. Next, Chapter 5: mapping data flows — real, visual, Spark-powered transformation, well beyond what a Copy activity alone can do.
